main_body: A three-storey red brick building with a flat gray roof seen from above, a cream cornice, rows of windows and an arched green double door
top_band: Light lavender-gray flat roof with slab joints and speckle, rows ~2-38, bordered by a pale parapet rim at rows ~36-40, then a cream cornice at rows ~42-46
evidence: Down the middle column the roof is a large, lighter, speckled horizontal surface with a chimney and a vent standing on it. A pale parapet edge at rows 36-40 marks the front edge, and the cream cornice at 42-46 sits over a dark maroon shadow row. The brick face below carries window sills, lintels and a recessed arched door. The roof is a real, clearly visible top surface, not a thin rim. The windows are only mildly inset, but the top, front edge, eave and front face are all present.

style.evidence: The brick has about 5 tones with per-brick variation and mortar rows. The roof slabs have speckle and joint lines. The cream trim has highlight and shadow steps. The windows have several blue and teal tones and glints. Outlines are dark maroon next to brick and tinted next to the other materials, not neutral black. The roof is a flat gray slab rather than a tiled pitched roof, but it is textured. Tiles carry many colours, comparable to the reference. It would sit next to the reference without looking thinner or flatter.
